newsitem.title: FRANCE: Police re-arrest suspect in Corsica car-bomb death.
newsitem.headline: Police re-arrest suspect in Corsica car-bomb death.

text.p: French police on Saturday re-arrested a freed suspect in the car-bomb killing of a Corsican nationalist leader on the Mediterranean resort island.
Police did not identify the man, released on a technicality earlier this week, but said he was to be flown to Paris within hours.
Police said they expected he would be placed under investigation for complicity in the July killing of a leader of of the Cuncolta Naziunalista movement in Bastia.
That attack was believed to be part of a war between rival separatist groups on the turbulent French-ruled island who disagree on objectives and tactics.
Police initially arrested the man and his brother after seizing dynamite and a heavy calibre revolver at the offices of a sports and cultural group.
They were released on Friday because authorities failed to file in time the correct documents needed to keep them under arrest. The brother was not re-arrested.
The Movement for Self-Determination (MPA), a rival of Cuncolta Naziunalista, denied in a statement that either man belonged to its ranks.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe has repeatedly pledged to crack down on Corsican guerrillas pushing for greater autonomy from Paris, but few have been detained.
